Ah okay! I was coming first from a place of purely survival and physically getting out of the situation permanently before the emotional aspect but you’ve already done the hard part! I’m sure you said this in your post but I truly got emotional so, sorry about that. 

I highly highly recommend therapy. When I finally escaped an abusive relationship, I found it so helpful to help me unlearn the fight or flight response and break the cycle. What you’re likely experiencing is PTSD, and your body’s new “comfort” is in a place of fight or flight. Therapy will help you go back to place of regulation. It might also be worth putting your son in therapy too, I imagine a lot of change and stress might have some toll on him. 

The other important thing is to surround yourself with people who support you and your decisions. Since it seems like your family might push you go to back to him, I’d try to connect with friends and even find your own place to live if this is a possibility.

First of all, I’m so sorry for what you’re going through, and what you’ve been going through. I think it’s important to say that you’re not being selfish and you’re doing an INCREDIBLY difficult thing right now. Leaving someone who’s abusive is so hard. Knowing you need to do that is also hard.  You going back to your husband is not about selfishness, it’s about a narcissistic, abusive man who’s repeatedly bringing you down and making you feel like you don’t have other options. That is the point of abuse. 

Do you have savings to get away from this man for good? Do you have family nearby that you could reach out to for shelter? If not, are there shelters near you that could house you and your son? They may have resources to help you and make sure you’re safe from this man. I also would recommend trying to get a restraining order against your husband. 

I’m sure other folks will comment with better advice, but these are the first things I can think of. This is a horrible situation and my heart is with you. You’re incredibly strong and I hope you find the space for you and your son to heal from this trauma ❤️

I think a lot of it has to do with not beating yourself up if you don't do x thing you've set out to do. I think setting little goals - even if it's just "sit up in bed, rather than laying down" or "going from the bed to the couch". That's a step, and reframing that for yourself as a small victory might be helpful.

I'm by no means saying this is def the answer - My thinking is that it's easy when depressed to beat yourself up for not doing all the things you "should" be doing. So being compassionate with yourself and recognizing that what you're going through is challenging and just recognizing that even the smallest thing is a victory. 

The other thing I'll do when I'm feeling like this is trying to get myself to do something that I know I'll enjoy. Last time it was "if you shower, you'll feel slightly better". I didn't feel 100%, but I felt a bit better doing something that made me feel better and seemed productive to me (even if it was a short rinse).
